title: India Thrash South Korea 8-1 to Reach Seventh Asian Champions Trophy Final
excerpt: Braces from Shilanand Lakra and Dilpreet Singh powered an 8-1 semi-final rout of South Korea in Mohali on Wednesday, setting up a title match against Japan on Thursday.
body:
• India beat South Korea 8-1 in the Asian Champions Trophy semi-final in Mohali on Wednesday to reach a record-extending seventh final in the tournament.
  • Shilanand Lakra (4th and 13th minutes) and Dilpreet Singh (21st and 25th) scored twice each, with captain Harmanpreet Singh, Sukhjeet Singh, Angad Bir Singh and Vivek Sagar Prasad adding one goal each; Sangjun Han scored South Korea's only goal.
  • India remain unbeaten in the tournament, having won all five league matches, including an 8-0 win over the same opponents in the league stage.
  • India face Japan in the final on Thursday, November 5, in Mohali; Japan beat Malaysia in a shootout after a goalless draw in the first semi-final.

India beat South Korea 8-1 in the semi-final of the men's Asian Champions Trophy in Mohali on Wednesday, reaching the final of the tournament for a record-extending seventh time, according to a PTI report carried by The Bridge. The result was India's second emphatic win over South Korea in three days, after an 8-0 victory in the final league match in Jalandhar on Monday.

India scored six times in the first 25 minutes

Shilanand Lakra opened the scoring in the fourth minute and struck again in the 13th, according to the PTI report. Captain Harmanpreet Singh scored in the ninth minute, and Sangjun Han pulled one back for South Korea in the same minute. Dilpreet Singh then scored in the 21st and 25th minutes, and Sukhjeet Singh also scored in the 21st minute, putting India 6-1 ahead inside the first 26 minutes on the reported scoring times.

Angad Bir Singh added a seventh goal in the 36th minute and Vivek Sagar Prasad completed the scoring in the 54th minute. South Korea did not score again after Han's goal.

The spread of scorers continued a pattern from the league stage. According to FIH reporting on the league phase, India scored 34 goals and conceded five in their five league matches, and Harmanpreet led the tournament scoring charts with nine goals at the end of that phase.

An unbeaten run to the final

India topped the six-team league with a maximum 15 points from five wins and a goal difference of +29, according to the FIH. Japan finished second with 10 points, Malaysia third with nine and South Korea fourth with six, which set up Wednesday's semi-final pairings when the tournament moved from Jalandhar to the Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium in Mohali.

The semi-final was a rematch on short rest. India and South Korea had met in the last league match on Monday, when Dilpreet scored twice in an 8-0 win. Wednesday's margin was one goal smaller, but the outcome was settled early: South Korea trailed by five goals before the half-hour mark on the reported scoring times.

Japan stand between India and the title

India will face Japan in the final on Thursday, November 5, in Mohali. Japan reached the final by beating Malaysia in a shootout after the two teams were locked goalless in regulation time in the first semi-final earlier on Wednesday, according to the PTI report.

Japan finished second in the league stage, behind India. The final is scheduled for the same Mohali venue that hosted both semi-finals, according to the FIH tournament schedule.
